title: Microinteraction SLA tradecard - lab notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a small lab run comparing latency vs unit-cost tradeoffs for microinteraction-style workloads (turns <= 40 tokens, strict p95/p99 goals). The goal is a concise tradecard we can fold into a console help-tip: when customers ask "I need 100ms p95 for short chat turns, how much will that cost and what knobs matter?"

Setup summary (short):
- Workloads simulated: 
  * micro-utterance (median prompt 12 tokens, response 18 tokens)
  * short-turn (prompt 25, resp 30)
  * tiny-command (prompt 6, resp 8)
- Model variants: small open-llm (7B q4), mid (13B q4), large (70B q4/8-bit fallback)
- Deployment surfaces: Hosted API (shared, autoscale), Dedicated (reserved A100 pool), Private-onprem (baremetal V100-like nodes).
- Measured metrics per-profile: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms), CPU/GPU utilization %, tokens/sec throughput, estimated $ per 1k queries (rough amortized cost using current pricing model).
- Duration: each run 30 minutes steady-state with 10-minute ramp; microburst test: 30s spike at 5x baseline QPS.

Key definitions used here:
- Query = single prompt+response cycle as observed by client.
- Tight microinteraction SLA = p95 <= 120 ms (customer-facing target).
- Unit cost = amortized infra + runtime overhead for 1k queries (does not include storage or egress).

Raw top-level observations (high level):
- For tiny-command workload, even small models meet p95 < 120ms on Dedicated with modest batching off (cost low). Hosted can hit p95 120-200ms depending on cold-penalty and tenant noise.
- For micro-utterance and short-turn, p95 behavior diverges: Dedicated sustained <120ms with higher cost; Private shows slightly higher p95 variability but lower per-query cost when nodes are well packed; Hosted shows best price-for-latency at low QPS but not predictable at spike.

ASCII comparative snapshot (p95 latency ms / $ per 1k queries):

Workload        | Hosted (shared)    | Dedicated (A100 pool) | Private (onprem)
----------------|--------------------|------------------------|-------------------
tiny-command    | 85 ms  / $1.8      | 60 ms  / $3.5          | 95 ms  / $1.5
micro-utterance | 190 ms / $3.2      | 110 ms / $5.6          | 130 ms / $2.4
short-turn      | 260 ms / $4.9      | 115 ms / $6.8          | 170 ms / $3.3

Notes on table: hosted price uses public shared-price buckets + observed tenant contention cost; Dedicated cost assumes committed A100 amortization and slack; Private cost assumes high pack factor (0.8) and lower cloud margin but includes ops overhead estimate.

p99 behavior and microbursts:
- In a 5x microburst, Hosted p99 ballooned 3x (+700 ms) due to admission pacing and cold-shed fallback to smaller kernels. Dedicated p99 rose ~30-50% (short queuing), Private p99 rose 40-70% but recovered faster when session-affinity and local prewarm were enabled.

Small sketch: p95 vs QPS curve (micro-utterance)
   p95(ms)
    300 |                     Hosted  ---\\\\             
    250 |                       \    |    \           
    200 |  Hosted -------------\\---|     \  Dedicated
    150 |                    Dedicated|      \         
    100 |  Private --------------      |       \       
     50 |                                |        \    
         0   10   50   100   300   500   QPS

Interpretation (sketch): hosted p95 climbs earliest as QPS increases because tenant noise + small slot preemption cause jitter. Dedicated holds p95 lowest up to its committed throughput; Private sits between but has lower marginal cost after fill.

Tradeoff bullets (what knobs move the dial):
- Quantization + kernel selection: best lever for cost with modest p95 impact for short responses. Moving from float to q4/q8 saves 30–60% cost but can add 5–25 ms p95 depending on sequence handling.
- Batching: large batching helps cost but increases p95 for microinteractions. For SLA target <120ms, limit batching window to <=8ms or batch-size <=4 for micro workloads.
- KV prefix caching: huge ROI for short-turn with repeated context (chat); cache hit reduces per-query compute by 40–70% and p95 by ~15–40 ms on average.
- Prefetch/tiling: predictive prefetch helps at the cost of extra warm capacity; useful when session arrival patterns are predictable.

Operational recommendations (for console guidance):
- If customer needs p95 <= 120ms and low variability, recommend Dedicated with (1) small batching window, (2) q4 quant profile for 13B choice, (3) KV caching enabled and pinned policy. Note cost implication and provide estimated $/1k using our calculator.
- If customer wants cost minimization with acceptable p95 ~150–200ms, Private-onprem with high packing plus q4 is best when they can tolerate ops overhead.
- Hosted API is strong for low-throughput and unpredictable customers; warn on p99 microburst exposure and show SLA caveats.

Open questions / follow-ups in lab:
- Repeat runs with response-streaming enabled (we only measured non-streamed responses). Hypothesis: streaming may improve client-observed p95 for larger responses but could increase server overhead for small-turns.
- Sweep quant profiles vs tiny-batching window (concrete curve missing for q5-like profiles).
- More realistic client-side RTTs in different regions (all runs here were within same cloud region).

Appendix: quick config snippets used in test harness (pseudo):
- arrival pattern: poisson mean=30 qps baseline, spike=150 qps for 30s
- model: redwood/13b-q4 (kernel set=fast-attn, kv-cache=on)
- batch config: window_ms=8, max_batch=8, prefer_prefetch=false
- metrics: client RTT (ms), server process latency (ms), gpu-util %, eviction-rate

Concluding note:
This is an experimental sketch intended to be easily digestible in the Console "Latency & Cost" flyout for microinteraction customers. Next step: produce two small visual tiles (p95 vs QPS + dollar per 1k line) and an interactive calculator entry.

Notes-to-self: file link -> CONFLUENCE-4851 (microinteraction playbook). Put a short checklist into the Console copy deck: "Dedicated, q4, KV cache, small-batch".
